CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Temanggung Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Temanggung.
4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Temanggung.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling rights carried out by families, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.
7. Protection of Women is all activities to guarantee and protect women and their rights, so that they can live with justice, in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
8. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or hardship for women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
10. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes or certain purposes.
12. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
13. Victim is a woman including Female Workers working abroad and children who experience suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of such violence.
14. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
15. Gender is the difference between men and women in roles, functions, rights, responsibilities, and behavior formed by social values, culture and customs of community groups that can change according to time and local conditions. Responsibilities and behavior formed by social values, culture and customs of community groups that can change according to time and local conditions.
16. Gender equality and justice is equal opportunity between men and women to participate in the development process, equal access to all forms of services, and have a balanced social and economic status.
17. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, budgeting, monitoring and evaluation of policies, programs is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, budgeting, monitoring and evaluation of policies, programs and development activities in the region
18. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group hereinafter abbreviated as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of Gender Mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region.
19. Integrated service is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of violence including criminal acts of trafficking in persons carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
20. Protection of Women is any act aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
21. legal act is any act or action of a legal subject that has legal consequences and the legal consequences are indeed desired by the legal subject.
22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
24. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a Complaint Center that provides integrated services for women and children victims of violence
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 34

1. Forms of Violence against Women include:a. physical violence;
b. sexual violence;
c. economic violence; andd. psychological violence.
2. The form of physical violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, unconsciousness and or causes death.
3. The form of sexual violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. The form of economic violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is the neglect of women in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.
5. The form of psychological violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Article 35

1. Every Victim of violence must receive Protection in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.
2. Protection of victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is provided to Regional Residents who experience violence in the Region or outside the Region.
3. Protection of victims of violence in addition to being provided to Regional residents as referred to in paragraph (2) is also provided to non-Regional residents that occurs in the Region.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TEMANGGUNG REGENCY

NUMBER 14 OF 2020

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage its own region for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of the Regional Government is to make a regional policy with the aim of improving the welfare of the people in its region.

In addition, the constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has also mandated in Article 28D Paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution that everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection, and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution also states that every child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to protection from violence and discrimination. This shows that women should be protected by the state, especially against violence because their rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Protection carried out by the Government for women is concretely implemented, namely by the issuance of Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), hereinafter abbreviated as CEDAW.

The government's efforts to protect its citizens, especially women, are also clearly implied in the provisions of Article 3 paragraph (2) of Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights which states that: "everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection and fair legal treatment and to obtain legal certainty and equal treatment before the law".

Violence and trafficking against women are already regulated in Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and violence against women, especially for the Temanggung Regency area. The Temanggung Regency Government is one of the most authorized parties in empowering women in order to provide guarantees for justice and gender equality, through efforts to build commitment to integrate gender-responsive budgets in programs and activities.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage improvement efforts on access, control, participation and benefits for justice and gender equality as well as the physical and mental conditions of women victims of violence.

Article 28

1. Every Victim has the right to receive Protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, both Regional Government and the community.
2. In the event of violence, every Victim has the right to receive health services and assistance, both psychologically and legally, and to receive guarantees of their rights related to their status as women.

Article 2

Point a What is meant by respect for Human Rights is respecting and upholding human rights law.

Point b What is meant by Gender Equality is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, social and cultural activities, Education and national defense and security, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Point c What is meant by Gender Justice is a process and fair treatment of women and men. Gender justice means there is no stereotyping of roles, double burden, subordination, marginalization and violence against women or men.

Point d What is meant by legal certainty is a principle in a state of law that prioritizes the foundation of laws and regulations, propriety, and justice in every policy of the State Organizer.

Article 3

Women's Empowerment and Protection aims to:
a. guarantee the fulfillment of women's rights so that they can live and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth; b. provide Gender Justice and Equality, improve the quality of life of women through increasing the institutional capacity of Women's Empowerment and Protection in the region, including the development of gender and child data systems; andc. provide protection of women's rights from various forms of violence and other discriminatory treatment.

Article 19

1. Women have the right to obtain special protection from things that threaten their safety and/or health.
2. Special protection is given to women because their reproductive function is guaranteed and protected by law.

CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

OF THE REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 15

1. The Regional Government is obliged and responsible for the implementation of women empowerment and protection.
2. Women empowerment and protection efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a. determination of policies, programs, and activities;
b. determination of implementation guidelines;
c. provision of services; and d. coordination of policies, programs and activities.
3. Women empowerment and protection efforts as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

NUMBER 14 OF 2020

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage its own region for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of the Regional Government is to make a regional policy with the aim of improving the welfare of the people in its region.

In addition, the constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has also mandated in Article 28D Paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution that everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection, and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution also states that every child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to protection from violence and discrimination. This shows that women should be protected by the state, especially against violence because their rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Protection carried out by the Government for women is concretely implemented, namely by the issuance of Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), hereinafter abbreviated as CEDAW.

The government's efforts to protect its citizens, especially women, are also clearly implied in the provisions of Article 3 paragraph (2) of Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights which states that: "everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection and fair legal treatment and to obtain legal certainty and equal treatment before the law".

Violence and trafficking against women are already regulated in Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and violence against women, especially for the Temanggung Regency area. The Temanggung Regency Government is one of the most authorized parties in empowering women in order to provide guarantees for justice and gender equality, through efforts to build commitment to integrate gender-responsive budgets in programs and activities.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage improvement efforts on access, control, participation and benefits for justice and gender equality as well as the physical and mental conditions of women victims of violence.

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage its own region for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of the Regional Government is to make a regional policy with the aim of improving the welfare of the people in its region.

In addition, the constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has also mandated in Article 28D Paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution that everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection, and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution also states that every child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to protection from violence and discrimination. This shows that women should be protected by the state, especially against violence because their rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Protection carried out by the Government for women is concretely implemented, namely by the issuance of Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), hereinafter abbreviated as CEDAW.

The government's efforts to protect its citizens, especially women, are also clearly implied in the provisions of Article 3 paragraph (2) of Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights which states that: "everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection and fair legal treatment and to obtain legal certainty and equal treatment before the law".

Violence and trafficking against women are already regulated in Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and violence against women, especially for the Temanggung Regency area. The Temanggung Regency Government is one of the most authorized parties in empowering women in order to provide guarantees for justice and gender equality, through efforts to build commitment to integrate gender-responsive budgets in programs and activities.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage improvement efforts on access, control, participation and benefits for justice and gender equality as well as the physical and mental conditions of women victims of violence.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage its own region for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of the Regional Government is to make a regional policy with the aim of improving the welfare of the people in its region.

In addition, the constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has also mandated in Article 28D Paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution that everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection, and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution also states that every child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to protection from violence and discrimination. This shows that women should be protected by the state, especially against violence because their rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Protection carried out by the Government for women is concretely implemented, namely by the issuance of Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), hereinafter abbreviated as CEDAW.

The government's efforts to protect its citizens, especially women, are also clearly implied in the provisions of Article 3 paragraph (2) of Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights which states that: "everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection and fair legal treatment and to obtain legal certainty and equal treatment before the law".

Violence and trafficking against women are already regulated in Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and violence against women, especially for the Temanggung Regency area. The Temanggung Regency Government is one of the most authorized parties in empowering women in order to provide guarantees for justice and gender equality, through efforts to build commitment to integrate gender-responsive budgets in programs and activities.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage improvement efforts on access, control, participation and benefits for justice and gender equality as well as the physical and mental conditions of women victims of violence.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage its own region for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of the Regional Government is to make a regional policy with the aim of improving the welfare of the people in its region.

In addition, the constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has also mandated in Article 28D Paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution that everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection, and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution also states that every child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to protection from violence and discrimination. This shows that women should be protected by the state, especially against violence because their rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Protection carried out by the Government for women is concretely implemented, namely by the issuance of Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), hereinafter abbreviated as CEDAW.

The government's efforts to protect its citizens, especially women, are also clearly implied in the provisions of Article 3 paragraph (2) of Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights which states that: "everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection and fair legal treatment and to obtain legal certainty and equal treatment before the law".

Violence and trafficking against women are already regulated in Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and violence against women, especially for the Temanggung Regency area. The Temanggung Regency Government is one of the most authorized parties in empowering women in order to provide guarantees for justice and gender equality, through efforts to build commitment to integrate gender-responsive budgets in programs and activities.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage improvement efforts on access, control, participation and benefits for justice and gender equality as well as the physical and mental conditions of women victims of violence.

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage its own region for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TEMANGGUNG REGENCY

NUMBER 14 OF 2020

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage its own region for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of the Regional Government is to make a regional policy with the aim of improving the welfare of the people in its region.

In addition, the constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has also mandated in Article 28D Paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution that everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection, and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution also states that every child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to protection from violence and discrimination. This shows that women should be protected by the state, especially against violence because their rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Protection carried out by the Government for women is concretely implemented, namely by the issuance of Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), hereinafter abbreviated as CEDAW.

The government's efforts to protect its citizens, especially women, are also clearly implied in the provisions of Article 3 paragraph (2) of Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights which states that: "everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection and fair legal treatment and to obtain legal certainty and equal treatment before the law".

Violence and trafficking against women are already regulated in Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and violence against women, especially for the Temanggung Regency area. The Temanggung Regency Government is one of the most authorized parties in empowering women in order to provide guarantees for justice and gender equality, through efforts to build commitment to integrate gender-responsive budgets in programs and activities.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage improvement efforts on access, control, participation and benefits for justice and gender equality as well as the physical and mental conditions of women victims of violence.

CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

OF THE REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 15

1. The Regional Government is obliged and responsible for the implementation of women empowerment and protection.
2. Women empowerment and protection efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a. determination of policies, programs, and activities;
b. determination of implementation guidelines;
c. provision of services; and d. coordination of policies, programs and activities.
3. Women empowerment and protection efforts as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 3

Women's Empowerment and Protection aims to:
a. guarantee the fulfillment of women's rights so that they can live and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth; b. provide Gender Justice and Equality, improve the quality of life of women through increasing the institutional capacity of Women's Empowerment and Protection in the region, including the development of gender and child data systems; andc. provide protection of women's rights from various forms of violence and other discriminatory treatment.

Article 16

1. In implementing policies, programs, and activities for women protection and women empowerment, the Regional Government may cooperate with the community/community institutions.
2. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage its own region for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of the Regional Government is to make a regional policy with the aim of improving the welfare of the people in its region.

In addition, the constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has also mandated in Article 28D Paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution that everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection, and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution also states that every child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to protection from violence and discrimination. This shows that women should be protected by the state, especially against violence because their rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Protection carried out by the Government for women is concretely implemented, namely by the issuance of Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), hereinafter abbreviated as CEDAW.

The government's efforts to protect its citizens, especially women, are also clearly implied in the provisions of Article 3 paragraph (2) of Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights which states that: "everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection and fair legal treatment and to obtain legal certainty and equal treatment before the law".

Violence and trafficking against women are already regulated in Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and violence against women, especially for the Temanggung Regency area. The Temanggung Regency Government is one of the most authorized parties in empowering women in order to provide guarantees for justice and gender equality, through efforts to build commitment to integrate gender-responsive budgets in programs and activities.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage improvement efforts on access, control, participation and benefits for justice and gender equality as well as the physical and mental conditions of women victims of violence.

Article 19

1. Women have the right to obtain special protection from things that threaten their safety and/or health.
2. Special protection is given to women because their reproductive function is guaranteed and protected by law.

Article 14

Every woman is obliged to:
a. uphold her dignity as a woman; b. carry out her duties and responsibilities as a wife, mother, child and member of society well and responsibly; and c. comply with the provisions of laws and regulations.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TEMANGGUNG REGENCY

NUMBER 14 OF 2020

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage its own region for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of the Regional Government is to make a regional policy with the aim of improving the welfare of the people in its region.

In addition, the constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has also mandated in Article 28D Paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution that everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection, and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution also states that every child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to protection from violence and discrimination. This shows that women should be protected by the state, especially against violence because their rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Protection carried out by the Government for women is concretely implemented, namely by the issuance of Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), hereinafter abbreviated as CEDAW.

The government's efforts to protect its citizens, especially women, are also clearly implied in the provisions of Article 3 paragraph (2) of Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights which states that: "everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection and fair legal treatment and to obtain legal certainty and equal treatment before the law".

Violence and trafficking against women are already regulated in Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and violence against women, especially for the Temanggung Regency area. The Temanggung Regency Government is one of the most authorized parties in empowering women in order to provide guarantees for justice and gender equality, through efforts to build commitment to integrate gender-responsive budgets in programs and activities.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage improvement efforts on access, control, participation and benefits for justice and gender equality as well as the physical and mental conditions of women victims of violence.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TEMANGGUNG REGENCY

NUMBER 14 OF 2020

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage its own region for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of the Regional Government is to make a regional policy with the aim of improving the welfare of the people in its region.

In addition, the constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has also mandated in Article 28D Paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution that everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection, and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution also states that every child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to protection from violence and discrimination. This shows that women should be protected by the state, especially against violence because their rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Protection carried out by the Government for women is concretely implemented, namely by the issuance of Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), hereinafter abbreviated as CEDAW.

The government's efforts to protect its citizens, especially women, are also clearly implied in the provisions of Article 3 paragraph (2) of Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights which states that: "everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection and fair legal treatment and to obtain legal certainty and equal treatment before the law".

Violence and trafficking against women are already regulated in Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and violence against women, especially for the Temanggung Regency area. The Temanggung Regency Government is one of the most authorized parties in empowering women in order to provide guarantees for justice and gender equality, through efforts to build commitment to integrate gender-responsive budgets in programs and activities.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage improvement efforts on access, control, participation and benefits for justice and gender equality as well as the physical and mental conditions of women victims of violence.

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage its own region for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of the Regional Government is to make a regional policy with the aim of improving the welfare of the people in its region.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage its own region for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of the Regional Government is to make a regional policy with the aim of improving the welfare of the people in its region.

In addition, the constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has also mandated in Article 28D Paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution that everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection, and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution also states that every child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to protection from violence and discrimination. This shows that women should be protected by the state, especially against violence because their rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Protection carried out by the Government for women is concretely implemented, namely by the issuance of Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), hereinafter abbreviated as CEDAW.

The government's efforts to protect its citizens, especially women, are also clearly implied in the provisions of Article 3 paragraph (2) of Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights which states that: "everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection and fair legal treatment and to obtain legal certainty and equal treatment before the law".

Violence and trafficking against women are already regulated in Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and violence against women, especially for the Temanggung Regency area. The Temanggung Regency Government is one of the most authorized parties in empowering women in order to provide guarantees for justice and gender equality, through efforts to build commitment to integrate gender-responsive budgets in programs and activities.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage improvement efforts on access, control, participation and benefits for justice and gender equality as well as the physical and mental conditions of women victims of violence.

Article 34

1. Forms of Violence against Women include:a. physical violence;
b. sexual violence;
c. economic violence; andd. psychological violence.

3. The form of sexual violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. The form of economic violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is the neglect of women in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.
5. The form of psychological violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage its own region for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of the Regional Government is to make a regional policy with the aim of improving the welfare of the people in its region.

In addition, the constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has also mandated in Article 28D Paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution that everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection, and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution also states that every child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to protection from violence and discrimination. This shows that women should be protected by the state, especially against violence because their rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Protection carried out by the Government for women is concretely implemented, namely by the issuance of Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), hereinafter abbreviated as CEDAW.

The government's efforts to protect its citizens, especially women, are also clearly implied in the provisions of Article 3 paragraph (2) of Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights which states that: "everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection and fair legal treatment and to obtain legal certainty and equal treatment before the law".

Violence and trafficking against women are already regulated in Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and violence against women, especially for the Temanggung Regency area. The Temanggung Regency Government is one of the most authorized parties in empowering women in order to provide guarantees for justice and gender equality, through efforts to build commitment to integrate gender-responsive budgets in programs and activities.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage improvement efforts on access, control, participation and benefits for justice and gender equality as well as the physical and mental conditions of women victims of violence.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage its own region for the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of the Regional Government is to make a regional policy with the aim of improving the welfare of the people in its region.

In addition, the constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has also mandated in Article 28D Paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution that everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection, and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution also states that every child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to protection from violence and discrimination. This shows that women should be protected by the state, especially against violence because their rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Protection carried out by the Government for women is concretely implemented, namely by the issuance of Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), hereinafter abbreviated as CEDAW.

The government's efforts to protect its citizens, especially women, are also clearly implied in the provisions of Article 3 paragraph (2) of Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights which states that: "everyone has the right to recognition, guarantees, protection and fair legal treatment and to obtain legal certainty and equal treatment before the law".

Violence and trafficking against women are already regulated in Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and violence against women, especially for the Temanggung Regency area. The Temanggung Regency Government is one of the most authorized parties in empowering women in order to provide guarantees for justice and gender equality, through efforts to build commitment to integrate gender-responsive budgets in programs and activities.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage improvement efforts on access, control, participation and benefits for justice and gender equality as well as the physical and mental conditions of women victims of violence.

5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling rights carried out by families, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.
7. Protection of Women is all activities to guarantee and protect women and their rights, so that they can live with justice, in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
8. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or hardship for women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
10. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes or certain purposes.
12. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
13. Victim is a woman including Female Workers working abroad and children who experience suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of such violence.
14. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
15. Gender is the difference between men and women in roles, functions, rights, responsibilities, and behavior formed by social values, culture and customs of community groups that can change according to time and local conditions. Responsibilities and behavior formed by social values, culture and customs of community groups that can change according to time and local conditions.
16. Gender equality and justice is equal opportunity between men and women to participate in the development process, equal access to all forms of services, and have a balanced social and economic status.
17. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, budgeting, monitoring and evaluation of policies, programs is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, budgeting, monitoring and evaluation of policies, programs and development activities in the region
18. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group hereinafter abbreviated as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of Gender Mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region.
19. Integrated service is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of violence including criminal acts of trafficking in persons carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
20. Protection of Women is any act aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
21. legal act is any act or action of a legal subject that has legal consequences and the legal consequences are indeed desired by the legal subject.
22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
24. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a Complaint Center that provides integrated services for women and children victims of violence
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
SUPPLEMENT TO THE REGIONAL GAZETTE OF TEMANGGUNG REGENCY NUMBER 120

CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

OF THE REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 15

1. The Regional Government is obliged and responsible for the implementation of women empowerment and protection.
2. Women empowerment and protection efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a. determination of policies, programs, and activities;
b. determination of implementation guidelines;
c. provision of services; and d. coordination of policies, programs and activities.
3. Women empowerment and protection efforts as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 16

1. In implementing policies, programs, and activities for women protection and women empowerment, the Regional Government may cooperate with the community/community institutions.
2. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER IX

MONITORING, EVALUATION, AND REPORTING

Article 39

Reporting on Women's Empowerment and Protection is conducted once (1) a year and coordinated by the Regional Apparatus in charge of women's empowerment affairs with the Province to the Minister who administers Government affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection through the Secretary of the Ministry.
